title: TeamTemplate
description: A team saved on this computer to use in any project: each agent's name, role, persona, picture and model, and the four answers setup asks. Stored as templates/<slug>.yaml in Catervas's state folder, readable by its owner alone. It leaves out everything that belongs to one project: rules, the criterion library, the preview, the integration branch, the team's name, and each agent's status, grants, revokes, preauthorized tools and connectors. See docs/SPEC.md section 3 and ADR 0026 (C).

name.description: What the user calls this saved team, with no space at either end. Its slug is the file's name.

agents.description: Each agent becomes an active one where the template is used. validate_template holds the team they make to validate_team's rules: unique ids, an active Product Manager and Software Developer, a named judge on the team.

id.description: A kebab-case slug of the display name, unique within the team. Events and contracts refer to an agent by it, so it never changes.

persona.description: A few lines of character added to the role's system prompt. It never grants anything.

avatar.description: The name of a shipped avatar. An uploaded picture, a path under .catervas/team/avatars/, is left out: nothing uploads one yet.

plan_in_sprints.description: Whether the team plans its work in sprints (ADR 0028). Left out, applying the template keeps the project's answer, and setup from it plans in sprints.

templatePolicy.description: Three of the four answers setup asks: what the agents may do, the plan check, and what happens to accepted work; and whether the team plans in sprints.

daily_usd.description: What the team may spend in a day before it pauses (spec 5.5). Left out, the day has no dollar limit: Catervas ships none (ADR 0015). A sprint's own budget belongs to the sprint, not here.

templateBudgets.description: The fourth answer, spending. Left out, the day has no dollar limit.

role.description: The role an agent is instantiated from. `human` is a role a contract may name as a reviewer, never a role an agent holds.

model.description: The agent's own model and effort. Either may be left out, and the role's stands in for it: changing how carefully an agent works never changes what it runs on.

id.description: The provider's model id, exactly as the runtime reports it in usage, so that the price table can be asked about it.

effort.description: How hard the model thinks. The runtime passes this value to the program as it is (catervas_runtime::SessionSpec::effort).

run_commands.description: Whether Developers and Architects run commands (the execute tier). Catervas still runs every check itself. Left out, true.

push.description: Whether Developers push and open pull requests (the git_remote tier). Left out, false.

permissions.description: The team's answers to what its agents may do, applied to every agent of the role before the agent's own grants and revokes (spec 5.6).

required.description: Whether every contract's plan is checked before work starts (spec 5.3). Left out, always.

default: Does the task fit its budget?
Would its checks notice if the work went wrong the way its intent worries about?
questions.description: What the judge answers about each plan, one answer per question. Left out, the two of spec 5.3. validate_team refuses none while required is always.

judge.description: Who checks plans. `auto` is the first active agent of the Architect, the Scrum Master and the Product Manager, in that order (the founder, 2026-09-29). A named judge must be an active agent (validate_team).

judgment.description: The plan check (spec 5.3). Left out, every plan is checked by the defaults.

integration.description: What happens to a task's branch after it is accepted (spec 5.14).
